cities.d: the vibrant, bustling capital city of the country. Predominantly French-speaking.

x.around: Bus trips are paid for using "Tap & Go" magnetic cards, just like in many public transport systems in the world. You can buy and reload the cards at newsstands and other points of sale. When boarding the bus, you pay for the ride by holding the card against the orange ticket machine next to the driver.

hidden.d: An artificial lake in the governmental quarters, the only real body of water in the city and another place to get away from the noise of the city.

A Chinese-built indoor arena, this is a venue for both team and individual sports from basketball to judo. It is also used for exhibitions, conferences and such events, moreover the building itself is a good example of futuristic…
Monument to the reunification of English and French Cameroon in 1961. Constructed in 1973, it's composed of the main monument, a statue of a man with his five children and a garden.
The club of the tennis player and singer Yannick Noah. It has a beautiful mid-sized pool and 4 tennis courts (3 full size and 1 half-size) in a park-like environment.
Located in a former Benedictine monastery. The three exhibition rooms presents traditional art such as masks, bronze and woodwork.
Built on the site of the first missionary church in Cameroon, it was consecrated in 2006, hence quite a modern building.

n.en: Mary Queen of the Apostles Basilica

hidden.d: Located in the former presidential palace, built during the French colonial period. This museum presents both traditional and modern aspects of Cameroon.
A museum showing traditional art from western and northwestern Cameroon; one of the highlights is the collections of the former royal treasury.

x.intro: Yaoundé is the capital of Cameroon, and the country's second most populous city. It is smaller than the economic centre (Douala), but still a bustling city. Called the city on seven hills, Yaoundé is home to people from all over Cameroon.

must.d: The seat of the Archdiocese of Yaoundé, built in 1951 and consecrated four years later. Nevertheless it is still reportedly under construction. With a cross-shaped interior, this cathedral has room for about 5,000 worshippers.

must.d: Memorial to an important Cameroonian historical figure who was the chief of Ewondo and Bane peoples and served diplomatically as an administrator with the German and French colonial powers for the betterment of the people.

next.d: a world heritage listed biosphere reserve, about 150 km southeast as the crow flies. Most likely you need a car to get there.
the largest city and economical centre of Cameroon, accessible by air, car, bus or train.

x.safe: While there are many more dangerous places in Cameroon and Africa than Yaoundé, crime can still be an issue here. Basic precautions will reduce the risk of you becoming victim.

x.around: All within-Bafoussam travel is provided by taxis or moto-taxis. Most destinations will tell you "what to say" to a taxi. Taxis are cheap; you can get halfway across Bafoussam for 100 FCFA.

hidden.d: An assortment of large boulders around which you may walk (rock grotto basically).
Waterfall on the Miti River, where nationalists were reportedly thrown to their deaths during colonial times and where sacrifices are made to ward off curses, etc. The water falls 40-50 m.

x.intro: Bafoussam is the capital of the West Region, in Northwest Highlands, Cameroon.

must.d: Chiefdom headquarters of Bandjoun: traditional huts first established by King Notouom I about four centuries ago, along with 'forest' and museum. A lot of history here.

hidden.d: A new cultural heritage museum and venue space.

must.d: Art and cultural museum describing the rich history of the Mankon fondom, a traditional kingdom. The museum is located in the former royal palace.

x.around: The main means of transportation are taxis. Motorbikes are allowed to circulate only within quarters.
x.intro: Buea is a city in Coastal Cameroon. It was the seat of German Cameroon in the beginning of the 20th century and still has some colonial buildings of interest. The city is at the foot of the active volcano Cameroon Mountain (Mongo ma Ndemi).

cities.d: the economical capital of the country. It handles Cameroon's international trade. Predominantly French-speaking.

hidden.d: Former estate of a noted anthropologist named Dika Akwa that shows elements of Sawa architecture and culture.
Housed in La Pagode, a structure that resembles a pagoda, showcases local artists' work and facilitates arts and culture in the community.

n.en: Cathedral of St Peter and Paul Bonadibong

hidden.d: Renowned statue made of recycled metal by Cameroonian artist Joseph-Francis Sumégnél in the 1990s that is supposed to express freedom.
Museum showcasing the rich maritime history of Douala.
old colonial type building, next to Doual'art and Parc Bonanjo across the street, which has a monument to an unknown soldier.

x.intro: Douala is the largest city and the commercial centre of Cameroon. Douala is really quite a hot and sticky place, and the grimy state of the infrastructure in parts leaves a lot to be desired. With more and more people coming here to seek a better life, it is struggling to keep up with issues like pollution and overcrowding. Sadly, it doesn't have a whole lot in the way of tourist attractions either, and prices tend to be elevated because of all the commerce and industry.

x.intro: Garoua is a port city lying on the Benue River in Northern Cameroon. Third biggest city in Cameroon.

cities.d: a peaceful coastal town with numerous black sand beaches. Predominantly English-speaking.

x.intro: Limbe is in the South West Region of Cameroon. It is a cosmopolitan city with a blend of various cultures which originated due to the hospitality of the people and western influence. This is one of the first cities in Cameroon to get in contact with the whites. The sanitation in Limbe is the best in Cameroon, so it has been nicknamed "clean city".

next.d: is an inland, neighbouring English-speaking city

x.safe: Limbe city is a safe city, with few incidents of harassment or theft. However, if you are the victim of any crime, do report it to the police, who will endeavour to solve the crime.

intro: Cameroon (French: Cameroun) is a country in Central Africa. Known as "Africa in miniature", the country is known for its geological, linguistic, artistic, and cultural diversity: some 250 languages are spoken in this mid-sized country. Cameroon was colonised by three European countries — Germany, France, and the United Kingdom.
